help.business-note.step1: Domestic › Loads, then open the load. Consignment note opens the note in a slide-up, page by page as it will print, with Print under it — “Save as PDF” in the print screen keeps it as a file. Once the note is kept, Share there sends a link to it, never the file.
help.business-note.step2: Once the carrier has taken the goods over, press Download this note and its photographs. You get one file: the note, every copy of it as it was signed, and its photographs. On a phone the button says Share, and opens your phone’s own share sheet.
help.business-note.step3: To give the note to somebody with no account, open “Papers” on the load, look under Links to this note and press Make a link to pass on. Then press Send it or Copy it, and send the link in a chat, a text or your own mail. The link is shown only once, because we keep no copy of it.
help.business-note.step4: To stop a link, press Cancel it on its row, then Yes, cancel it. A cancelled link cannot be switched back on. The row then says who cancelled it.
help.business-note.note1: When a load is delivered, the person who posted it is emailed a receipt at their own recovery email, with a button: Get the consignment note. If that person has left the business, or has given no email address, the owners are emailed instead.
help.business-note.note2: The button in the email is a link like the others. It is listed under Links to this note, with the address it went to, how often the file was taken, and until when it works.
help.business-note.note3: When somebody is taken out of the business, or leaves it, the links that were emailed to them stop at once. The same happens when somebody changes their own recovery email: the links sent to the old address stop. Links made for the business to pass on keep working until you cancel them.
help.business-note.note4: A link opens the note without signing in, for whoever has it. It works for 30 days and hands the file over 25 times at most. A note can have five links that work at the same time. Cancel one to make another.
help.business-note.note5: The price in the receipt is the price you and the carrier agreed. SeeBuyGet holds no money for your loads, and the receipt is not an invoice.
help.business-note.note6: A viewer sees the links and can download the file, but cannot make or cancel a link.
help.business-note.note7: If your own link stopped because you changed your email address, open the load and make a new one. The note itself is still there.
help.business-runs.title: Book space on a carrier’s run
help.business-runs.summary: Trucks that are leaving anyway, with room for your goods. The price is the carrier’s own, and you pay them directly.
help.business-runs.step1: “Domestic › Space on runs” lists the runs with room: where they go, when they leave, the carrier’s rate, and how they want to be paid.
help.business-runs.step2: Open one, say what you are sending and its weight, and ask what it would cost. Book it for that price.
help.business-runs.step3: Your bookings are listed above the runs. Open one for its consignment note, its tracking link, or to give the space back.
help.business-runs.step4: The tracking link opens a page anybody can read without an account: booked, on the road from the moment the carrier marks the run gone, then delivered and to whom. Send it to whoever is receiving the goods. It shows no price, and nobody else’s goods on the same truck.
help.business-contracts.title: Order from a carrier under contract
help.business-contracts.summary: If a fleet carries for you under a contract, your loads can go straight to that fleet instead of onto the open board.
help.business-contracts.step1: Your carrier records the contract in their fleet app and sends you a code. An owner opens Carriers, under Partners (on a phone, under More), pastes it and taps Link it. The code works once.
help.business-contracts.step2: When you post a load, choose that carrier under Who carries it, and the day it must arrive. Tomorrow is filled in for you.
help.business-contracts.step3: The load shows as With your carrier until they put it on a truck. Once your carrier has accepted its plan for that day, the load also says about when it is planned to arrive. Its tracking link and consignment note work the same as any other load.
help.business-contracts.note1: The price and how you pay are on your own contract with the carrier. SeeBuyGet keeps the order, the note and the tracking — never the money.
help.business-contracts.note2: An owner can end a contract under Carriers. Loads already ordered are still delivered.
help.business-contracts.note3: An order that is more than one vehicle carries may be brought in several loads by your carrier. You are told under the bell, each load says Load 1 of 2 in your list, and either tracking link shows them all.
help.business-contracts.note4: If your carrier’s plan for the day has a load arriving outside the delivery window you asked for, you are told under the bell, and the load says Outside your window with about when it is planned and by how much. A plan’s time is an estimate and your carrier can still plan the day again. If it cannot work, speak to your carrier.
help.business-contracts.note5: If your carrier’s plan for the day leaves a load on no vehicle, you are told under the bell, and the load says Not on a vehicle with the reason: no room that day, no vehicle that can carry it, heavier than their largest vehicle, or a place that could not be found on the map. Speak to your carrier, because the day can still be planned again. You are told again when the load is on a vehicle.
help.business-contracts.note6: The time a load is planned for is your carrier’s estimate. You see it in the Business app as soon as your carrier accepts its plan. Whoever holds the tracking link sees the day from the start, and about when only once the load is on the road.
help.business-contracts.note7: When a load is delivered, the notice and the load say what time it was handed over and whether that was inside the window you asked for: inside it, how long after it, or how long before. The time is on your carrier’s own clock.
help.business-contracts.note8: If a load has not arrived half an hour after the time your carrier planned, you are told under the bell that it is running late, and the load says Running late. You are told once more if its whole day passes. A plan’s time is an estimate, so this is a reason to ring your carrier, not proof that something is wrong.
help.business-contracts.note9: If a load is for today and your carrier has it on no vehicle once the day’s work has begun — seven in the morning on your carrier’s clock — you are told under the bell, and the load says Not on a vehicle. That is a day your carrier has not planned, a load ordered after the plan was made, or a load that missed its trip. A load ordered for the same day is given an hour first. You are told again when it is on a vehicle, whether your carrier planned the day again or put it on a driver by hand.
help.business-clients.title: Send for your clients as their agent
help.business-clients.summary: An expeditor keeps a book of the businesses it sends for. A load or a booking made for one of them names the client as the sender, and you as their agent.
help.business-clients.step1: “Clients › Add a client”: their registered name, country, address and who to ask for.
help.business-clients.step2: When you post a load or book space, choose the client under Sent for. They become the sender on the consignment note; you are named as the agent who booked it.
help.business-clients.step3: Open a client to see everything sent for them — loads and space on runs alike — with each one’s tracking link to hand them. It needs no account.
help.business-clients.step4: A client you no longer work for can be archived. What was sent for them keeps naming them.
help.business-clients.note1: Several clients’ goods on one run are several bookings on that run, one for each client — each with its own consignment note.
help.quotations.title: Keep track of a quotation and its payment
help.quotations.summary: Wherever a price lives — a clearing agent’s fee, a carrier’s price — SeeBuyGet keeps the quotation, the proforma invoice and whether it is paid, in one place. It never handles the money.
help.quotations.step1: A clearing agent quotes their fee on the import or the export, with their own quotation number. The importer or exporter agrees it.
help.quotations.step2: For a load — under “Payment” on the load — or a booking, press Keep track of paying the carrier: the agreed price is filled in, and you can change it to what the carrier invoiced.
help.quotations.step3: Either side can attach the proforma invoice. It is kept as it was handed over.
help.quotations.step4: When it is paid, press Confirm it is paid and add the payment’s reference if you have one. Set back to open undoes it.
help.quotations.note1: Every change is kept with the name of whoever made it, so “who said this was paid” can always be answered.
help.shop-shelves.title: Set up your pickup shelves
help.shop-shelves.summary: Every parcel that arrives for collection is given a slot of its own, named by a colour and a number, such as Red-2. The shop says how many rows and colour columns it has.
help.shop-shelves.step1: Shop app, My shop, “Set up shelves”. Rows are numbered and each column is a colour. Choose how many of each you have, then “Save shelf”.
help.shop-shelves.step2: One parcel off the bus: when you mark it arrived, the app names its slot. Put it there.
help.shop-shelves.step3: A bag: after “Receive and shelve” the app lists every slot and the parcels that go in it, under “Put each parcel in its slot”. Press “All on the shelf” when they are in.
help.shop-shelves.step4: When the customer comes, the app shows the same slot. A slot can be found again under Hand out, beside each parcel that is waiting.
help.shop-shelves.step5: Tap an empty slot to make it a bundle slot. Letters and small parcels then share it, up to twelve, instead of each taking a whole slot.
help.shop-shelves.note1: A bag goes onto the shelf whole or not at all. If there is no room for every parcel in it, the bag is refused and nothing is shelved: hand over parcels that are waiting, or add a row, then scan the bag again. One parcel that finds no slot stays with the driver in the same way.
help.shop-shelves.note2: A slot that holds a parcel cannot be taken away. Hand the parcel over first, or keep the shelf large enough for that slot. The app says which slot and which parcel.
help.shop-shelves.note3: A shelf has at least 6 slots and at most 10 colour columns, because every column is a colour of its own.
help.shop-shelves.note4: A slot is free again the moment its parcel is collected. A parcel with a problem reported at your counter keeps its slot, and can still be handed over.
help.shop-shelves.note5: Before you take a parcel in, the app says what covers it. “Carried by …, and not insured by it” means the company pays no claim itself: tell the customer, and tick the box that says you did. If something goes wrong they get a damage claim report to take to their own insurer.
help.shop-shelves.note6: A business’s parcel on its way to one of the business’s own places is shelved as usual, and listed under Hand out, in “For a business’s own door”. Keep it on the shelf until a driver has taken its load, then hand it only to that driver: “Scan their pass”, then “Hand it over”.
help.message-shop.title: Message a shop or a customer
help.message-shop.summary: Somebody collecting a parcel and the shop holding it can message each other about it, inside SeeBuyGet.
help.message-shop.step1: Send app: My parcels, open the parcel, then “Message the shop”. Say when you are coming, or ask when they are open.
help.message-shop.step2: Shop app: “Hand over a parcel › Waiting to be collected › Message” beside the parcel.
help.message-shop.step3: The shop can only reach a customer who has signed in to the Send app with the phone number they gave the store. If there is nobody to reach, the app says so.
help.message-shop.note1: Only the two of you can read it, and nothing in it can be edited or deleted. The collection code is never sent in a message — it stays on the parcel in the Send app.
help.message-shop.note2: A photo is never sent loose in the chat: it is filed to the parcel — as damage, a paper or proof — and the chat shows a card pointing to it. The shop, the person collecting the parcel and its sender can open it.
help.thermal-labels.title: Print labels on paper or a thermal printer
help.thermal-labels.summary: Every label prints on paper from the page it opens, or on a thermal label printer — the 100 × 150 mm kind couriers use — from a file.
help.thermal-labels.step1: Shop app: after taking a parcel in, “Open and print the label” opens it in a slide-up, on its page as it prints, with Print under it; “Thermal printer (ZPL)” saves it as a file for a label printer.
help.thermal-labels.step2: Store app: the same two once an order is paid — and again later, from the order under Orders: “Print the label again”, which opens the same slide-up, or “Thermal printer (ZPL)”. The Hub app prints a called-off parcel’s new label the same way.
help.thermal-labels.step3: Business app: Domestic › Loads, open the load, then “Papers”, under Papers for the goods: “Print labels” for paper — it opens in a slide-up, one label a page as it prints, with Print under it — and “Thermal printer (ZPL)” for a file with one label a package.
help.thermal-labels.step4: Send the file to the printer as it is: with the printer maker’s own tool (for a Zebra, Zebra Setup Utilities: “Open printer tools › Action › Send file”), or to the label printer shared on your computer.
help.thermal-labels.note1: The file is written for a 203 dpi printer loaded with 100 × 150 mm labels. Set the label size on the printer first: a printer set to another size prints it cut off.
help.thermal-labels.note2: A label never carries the code that releases a parcel — only its public tracking key.
help.bag-seals.title: Close, take and receive a sealed bag
help.bag-seals.summary: A bag leaves closed — with a coded seal, its number typed and the bag photographed, or photographed closed without one — and the driver taking it, and whoever receives it, read the seal and photograph it: the driver before it goes, the receiver before opening it.
help.bag-seals.step1: Shop app, in Bag parcels: before “Close the bag”, choose a coded seal (suggested), pull it tight through the zip, type its number as printed and photograph the bag with the seal in view — or, without a seal, photograph the bag closed.
help.bag-seals.step2: Hub app, in Load a bag: a bag not yet closed is closed the same way before the driver’s badge is scanned. Store app, on your dock: “Close the bag” asks the same.
help.bag-seals.step3: A bag that is not closed is not loaded: the app says “Close the bag first”.
help.bag-seals.step4: Driver app, in My loads: taking a bag yourself, read the number off its seal (it is never shown to you), photograph the bag as you take it and say it is as it was closed. A number that is not the one it was closed with is said on the spot, signal or not.
help.bag-seals.step5: A bag a shop or hub loads onto you by the pass on your phone: under My loads, “Read its seal”. It is received nowhere until you have; with no signal, your reading waits on your phone and goes when there is signal.
help.bag-seals.step6: Receiving — Shop app, Receive a bag; Hub app, Drop a bag: scan it, read the number off its seal (it is never shown to you), photograph it as it arrived, and say whether it is as it was closed. Only then is it opened.
help.bag-seals.step7: A number that is not the one it was closed with: read it again; still not the same, “Still not the same? Report it”. A broken seal or a cut bag: “Cut, opened or the seal broken”, then report it. The bag is held and SeeBuyGet operations told; it is received once operations releases it.
help.bag-seals.step8: A bag you take or carry that is not right: “Something is not right with this bag”. It is held where it is and SeeBuyGet operations told.
help.bag-seals.note1: One coded seal closes one bag: a number already on a bag still travelling is refused. Seals and label printers are not sold in SeeBuyGet.
help.held-on-the-road.title: Report being held by police or customs
help.held-on-the-road.summary: Say it from the load in the Driver app: SeeBuyGet operations, the shipper and your fleet’s office are told at once, and again when you are let go.
help.held-on-the-road.step1: Driver app, My loads: under a load on the road, “Held by police or customs?”. Choose who holds it — the police, customs or somebody else — and, if you can, who and where (“Traffic police, Athi River”) and what they said or want. Then “Say it — operations is told”.
help.held-on-the-road.step2: The load’s card says it is held, since when, and that operations, the shipper and your office have been told — and the number of the desk to ring, for the country the load was taken over in and the one it goes to. Tap it to ring. With no signal it waits on your phone, dated when you said it, and goes when there is signal; the desk numbers are on your phone already.
help.held-on-the-road.step3: It is not delivered while it is held. When you drive on, “Let go — we drive on”.
help.held-on-the-road.step4: Business app: the load says “Held by an authority”, by whom and since when, until it is let go; you are told both times in your bell, and your system hears load.held and load.let_go.
help.held-on-the-road.note1: The tracking page, which anybody with the label’s key reads, says only that the load is held on the way and since when: never by whom or where, and never where your phone is. A vehicle held where its driver said it is held is not a vehicle standing still for no reason.
help.load-seals.title: Seal a load before pickup
help.load-seals.summary: Where you seal a load, you write each seal in the Business app before the goods are taken over. The driver reads each one off the door at pickup, and every seal is recorded against what it closes: the container and the load’s package codes.
help.load-seals.step1: Open the load in the Business app, then “Papers”, and go to Seals. Before pickup, press Write a seal: its number as printed on it, its class as marked (ISO 17712: H, S or I), the maker if it shows one, and who closed it — your own seal, or customs.
help.load-seals.step2: Take the three photographs as you seal it: the load open, blocked and braced; the doors closed with the vehicle’s or container’s number and the seal in view; the seal close up, its whole number readable. Then press Write the seal.
help.load-seals.step3: Each seal is kept with what it closes: the container the load names and the load’s package codes (SSCC), as they are when you write it. Its line says so — on container …, over the packages labelled for this load — and the consignment note says it too.
help.load-seals.step4: At pickup the driver reads each seal off the door and photographs it. A number that is not the one you wrote and the load does not leave.
help.load-seals.step5: After pickup the seals stay on the record: one customs replaced at a post, one found broken on the road, and the look at the door at delivery are all said on the seal’s line.
help.load-seals.note1: The driver is never shown a seal’s number before pickup: they read it off the door, so a number looked up cannot stand in for one read.
help.load-seals.note2: Whether a seal is required is the rule of the company of the country your goods are taken over in: on loads that cross a border, on container legs, or not at all. Where it is required, Seals says so and names the company, and the goods are not taken over until a seal is written. Where it is not, a seal is your choice; where you seal a load, write every seal on it.
help.tampering.title: Hold and report goods that look opened
help.tampering.summary: Whatever looks opened is held where it is: photographed, reported, and changing hands with nobody until SeeBuyGet operations has looked and released it.
help.tampering.step1: Driver app, at pickup: a seal read off the door that is not the number written — read it again; still not the same, tap “Still not the same? Report it”, photograph the seal as it is, and send.
help.tampering.step2: Driver app, on the road or at the door: “Something is not right with this load” for a cut wrap; at the receiver’s, say the seals are not as the note says and report them first. A seal found broken on the road is reported as before, and holds the load too.
help.tampering.step3: Shop app: the job “Packaging cut or opened” — scan the parcel, photograph it as it is, report it. Hub app: on the sort screen, “Packaging cut or opened? Report it”.
help.tampering.step4: While it is held: keep it closed, set it apart, do not open it further. It goes into no bag, onto no bus and to nobody; the app refuses each of these and says why.
help.tampering.step5: Console: the case “Held: tampering found” shows what was found, by whom, the photographs and the SSCC. Release it once you know what happened, with what was found and done: the case closes with those words.
help.tampering.note1: Operations is told at once, and the shipper or the store whose goods they are; the receiver is never texted. With no signal the report waits on the phone with its photograph and goes when it can.
help.tampering.note2: A release judges nothing: it lets the goods move again. What was found stays on the record and on the consignment note, never with the name of who found it.
help.scan-a-parcel.title: Scan a parcel by QR or store barcode
help.scan-a-parcel.summary: A parcel’s box at the counter or the hub takes our QR — or, on a store’s parcel, the GS1-128 barcode under SSCC on its label. Either finds the same parcel.
help.scan-a-parcel.step1: Shop app: in Take in, Hand over, Bag and Hand out, scan our QR on the label as always — or the barcode under SSCC on a store’s parcel. The parcel’s code fills the box, and the screen goes on as with the QR.
help.scan-a-parcel.step2: Hub app: at the sort, the same — either code on the label finds the parcel standing at the hub.
help.scan-a-parcel.step3: A barcode that names no parcel this shop or hub is handling says so: scan our QR on the label instead.
help.scan-a-parcel.step4: A load’s package barcode finds its load, where this app opens loads.
help.scan-a-parcel.note1: A store’s barcode finds only parcels this shop is taking in or handing out, or that stand at this hub — or that a store booked to hand in at this hub, in bulk: to anyone else it names nothing, so it is never a way to look through a store’s parcels.
help.hub-bulk.title: Hand parcels in at a hub, in bulk
help.hub-bulk.summary: A store with many parcels can bring them to a hub on pallets or in cartons, on a day the hub receives. The hub counts what came at its door and scans each parcel in: from that scan the parcel is the hub’s to sort.
help.hub-bulk.step1: Hub app, Coming in: the hub’s owner taps “Take parcels in bulk” and says the days and hours it receives, on its own clock, and how many arrivals it can unload at once — and what it charges for each pallet, carton, cage or sack; a kind left blank is free. “Stop taking parcels in bulk” stops new bookings; what stores booked already still comes.
help.hub-bulk.step2: Store app, Ship: where the parcel starts, a hub that takes parcels in bulk is offered beside the shops, priced from the hub — no shop and no road before it.
help.hub-bulk.step3: Store app, Dock, under “To a hub, in bulk”: “Book an arrival”. Tick its parcels, say what they come on — pallets, cartons, cages or sacks — and how many, choose a day the hub receives, and add your own reference and who brings it. The units are paid from your balance when you book; any not counted at the door come back.
help.hub-bulk.step4: Hub app, Coming in: what is due today is under “At the door today”. Open it, count what came, add anything you saw, and tap “Taken in at the door”.
help.hub-bulk.step5: Then scan each parcel in: our QR, its tracking key or the store’s barcode. A code not on this arrival is refused — set that parcel aside, and tell the store. A parcel cut or opened: scan it in, then report it.
help.hub-bulk.step6: The last parcel ends the arrival. Some not there? “Done: the rest did not come”: they stay the store’s, and the store is told. What was scanned in waits with the other parcels to sort.
help.hub-bulk.step7: An arrival whose day has gone with nothing at the door: open it and tap “It did not come”. The store is told, and books its parcels again.
help.hub-bulk.note1: The store sees each arrival on its Dock: taken in, what was not there, and what the hub noted at its door. Its own system hears how each arrival ended.
help.hub-bulk.note2: Until a parcel is scanned in it is still the store’s: the hub answers for what it scanned in, not for what was booked.
help.gs1-codes.title: Put your own GS1 barcodes on labels
help.gs1-codes.summary: With the GS1 company prefix GS1 gave you, each of your parcels or packages gets its own SSCC, printed as a GS1-128 barcode beside our QR: what a receiving warehouse scans into its own system.
help.gs1-codes.step1: Store app: “My store › GS1 barcodes on your parcels › Give your GS1 prefix”: the company prefix GS1 gave you, and an extension digit your own systems do not use.
help.gs1-codes.step2: Business app: Business details, the GS1 panel — the same, for the loads you post. A forwarder gives a client’s own prefix on the client’s record.
help.gs1-codes.step3: From then on each store parcel, once it is paid for, and each package of a load gets its SSCC: on the printed label, on the thermal label, on the order, and in the shipping API’s answer as “sscc”.
help.gs1-codes.step4: Refused because another business or store prints under that prefix with that digit? If the prefix is yours, tap “This prefix is ours” and send a photograph or a screenshot of your GS1 licence. Those using it are told at their bell and have a week to send theirs; two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide whose it is, and everybody reads why.
help.gs1-codes.note1: We never make a prefix up: only GS1 gives one. No code is ever given twice, and a parcel or a load keeps the codes it was given if you change the prefix or stop.
help.gs1-codes.note2: At our shops and hubs a store parcel’s barcode finds its parcel, as our QR does; it is also what the warehouse receiving the goods scans into its own system.
help.no-signal.title: Work with no signal
help.no-signal.summary: The app keeps working on what it last knew, and records the parcels you move. Some things wait for a connection.
help.no-signal.step1: Taking a parcel in, handing it to the bus, shelving it, moving a bag: recorded on the phone at once, dated when you did it, and sent when the signal returns. A line at the top counts what is still to send.
help.no-signal.step2: What you see is what the app last loaded, and the line at the top says so, with the time.
help.no-signal.step3: Your collection code stays on your phone once the parcel has appeared in My parcels — open the app once while you have signal.
help.no-signal.step4: Signing in, paying and handing a parcel over at the counter need a connection, and so do a price, an agreement and a voice message in a chat. The app says so plainly when it cannot do them.
help.no-signal.step5: Drivers: ending your shift is recorded on the phone too. Starting one and taking an offer need a connection; an offer you could not see lapses after ten minutes and is not held against you. The fleet app shows when each vehicle was last heard from.
help.no-signal.step6: Drivers: the consignment note of each load that is yours is kept on your phone while there is signal, so it opens at a checkpoint with none — it says it is the copy kept, and when. Notes of loads no longer yours, and all of them when you sign out, are removed. Across a border the load’s commercial invoice is kept beside its note, from pickup on, and removed with it.
help.no-signal.note1: Do not clear the app’s data while something is still to send: the record of what you moved is on the phone until it has gone.
help.no-signal.note2: A parcel or bag moved, a load picked up or delivered, a border passed, a temperature read, a breakdown or a road hazard, a shift ended: sent later, each keeps the time you did it, by the phone’s clock — never a time still to come, never more than a week back, and never before the step before it. A shift’s end is never dated before your phone was last heard from on that shift. Where its time is written down, such as the damage claim report or the consignment note, it says when SeeBuyGet heard of it too.
help.no-signal.note3: A chat message written with no signal waits on the phone, and goes by itself when the signal comes back. The other side reads when you wrote it and when it arrived, so a message that arrives late is not taken as new. A photo filed with no signal waits the same way.
help.consignment-note.title: The consignment note (CMR)
help.consignment-note.summary: Every load carries one document from posting to delivery, in the CMR layout: sender, consignee, carrier and vehicle, the goods, taking over and delivery. Across a border it says which law the carriage is under: the CMR where either country is a party to it, the Northern Corridor’s road protocol between its members, or else its contract.
help.consignment-note.step1: Shop app: Freight, open the load, then “Consignment note”. It opens in a slide-up, page by page as it will print. Print opens the phone’s print screen; choose “Save as PDF” there to keep it for your books. On an iPhone, “Open to print” opens it on a page of its own: tap Share, then Print.
help.consignment-note.step2: Driver app: “Loads › Consignment note” under the load — show it at a weighbridge, a border or the receiver’s gate. “Actual size” shows the page as large as it prints, to read from the phone.
help.consignment-note.step3: Driver app, across a border: once you have taken the goods over, “Commercial invoice” is under the load beside the note — the paper the officer asks for. It is not shown before pickup, nor on a load in one country, nor to your fleet’s office: it is the shipper’s paper.
help.consignment-note.step4: Fleet app: “Earnings › Consignment note” on any haul.
help.consignment-note.note1: Every box is filled from a recorded act — posting, the load-safety check at pickup, the unload report at delivery. A box that says “not recorded” is not recorded; nothing is typed in by hand. The buyer of a store order is named as the buyer, never by phone number.
